s.note: Crisp, hollow choux puffs baked with gruyere, dijon and black pepper, served warm
s.how: Heat the oven to 200C. Bring 125ml water, 125ml milk, 100g butter and 1/2 tsp salt to the boil, tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat for 2 minutes until it comes away from the pan. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time, then 120g grated gruyere, 1 tsp dijon and pepper. Pipe or spoon walnut-sized balls onto lined trays, scatter with 30g more gruyere and bake 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Serve warm.

s.note: Hot-smoked trout folded with butter, crème fraîche, lemon, chives and capers, with toasted baguette and cornichons
s.how: Flake 300g hot-smoked trout, checking for bones. Mash with 150g softened butter, 100g crème fraîche, the zest and juice of 1 lemon, chopped chives, 1 tbsp chopped baby capers and white pepper, leaving it coarse. Pack into a dish, smooth the top and chill for 1 hour. Serve with slices of toasted baguette and cornichons.

m.n: The new patron's steak frites with bearnaise
m.note: Seared sirloin with double-fried chips, watercress and a warm tarragon and shallot bearnaise
m.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips, rinse, dry and fry at 140C for 8 minutes in batches until soft but pale. Simmer 3 tbsp white wine vinegar, 1 chopped shallot, half the tarragon and 2 tbsp water down to 1 tbsp and strain. Whisk with 2 egg yolks in a bowl over simmering water until thick, then whisk in 180g melted butter in a thin stream and add the rest of the tarragon. Rub 4 sirloin steaks with oil, salt and pepper and sear in a very hot pan for 3 minutes a side for medium rare, then rest 5 minutes. Fry the chips again at 190C until crisp and salt them. Serve the steaks with chips, bearnaise and watercress.

w.note: Baked vanilla and rosewater custard over crushed raspberries, chilled and topped with a crackling burnt sugar crust
w.how: Heat the oven to 150C. Warm 500ml thickened cream with 1 split vanilla bean until steaming. Whisk 6 egg yolks with 80g caster sugar, pour in the hot cream, then stir in 1 tsp rosewater and strain. Crush 100g raspberries into the base of 4 ramekins, pour over the custard and bake in a water bath for 35 minutes until just set with a wobble. Cool, then chill at least 4 hours. Just before serving, scatter 1 tbsp caster sugar over each and burn with a blowtorch or under a very hot grill until glassy. Top with a few rose petals if you have them.

d.note: Blackcurrant liqueur topped with chilled dry sparkling wine in a flute, with fresh blackberries
d.how: Chill a bottle of dry sparkling wine and 4 flutes. Pour 20ml blackcurrant liqueur into each flute, top slowly with the sparkling wine and drop in a few blackberries.
